newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries well bid in quiet London, await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries well bid in quiet London, await FOMC.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London were slightly higher on Wednesday but analysts said there would be little activity ahead of any decision on interest rates from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

An announcement is expected around 1815 GMT but the Fed was largely expected to leave interest rates steady. The market would then immediately turn its attention to the June employment report on Thursday, they said.
"The market will be quiet until after the results of the FOMC are known. But the market will maintain a decent bid," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The 30-year benchmark T-bond was at 98-19 at 0938 GMT, yielding 6.733 percent, up from 98-15 in Tokyo and 98-16 at the New York close on Tuesday.
Two-year T-notes were at 99-31, up slightly from 99-30 at the Tokyo and New York closes, while five-year notes were at 99-24 up two ticks from the Tokyo and New York closes.
The trader said there had been general buying of the dollar bloc.
"There has been some decent buying in the long end and some swap related buying of the five-year sector," he trader said.
The only data due on Wednesday were May factory orders figures at 1400 GMT. They were forecast to fall 0.2 percent compared with a 1.2 percent rise in April.
"While people will be looking at those numbers the market is likely to remain quiet ahead of the FOMC announcement and the employment report," he said.
Sonja Gibbs, senior bond strategist at Nomura International in London agreed.
"Even if we get an upside surprise on factory orders the market is going to overlook it ahead of the FOMC because the June NAPM looked softer," she said.
On Tuesday the National Association of Purchasing Management survey fell to 55.7 from 57.1 in May.
But Gibbs said the employment component was up in both the NAPM and the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index, skewing the risk to the upside for the headline figure on non-farm payrolls.
For Wednesday, Gibbs said there might be a slight rally in Treasuries once the Fed announcement was known.
"It is so widely expected for the Fed to leave rates on hold that you wouldn't expect a lot of reaction, but we will get a bit of lift on relief," she said.
The market would also take note of the details of the five-year index linked auction, she said. They will be announced at 1830 GMT.
"If the amount is smaller than people anticipate it could be supportive to the market," she said.
September T-bond futures were at 111-27 in automated trade, up 5/32 from Tuesday's Chicago settlement.
